thread:
maya: Pushed v2.3-int4 to a 5% splitrail for chat. Quick smoke shows latency win but a worrying longdoc quality delta. Posting raw numbers.
alex: Can you drop the smoke table here?

maya: ```
model        | p95 latency | avg tok cost | longdoc MRR | halluc rate
v2.2-int8    | 210ms       | $0.009       | 0.82        | 0.9%
v2.3-int4    | 185ms       | $0.006       | 0.78        | 1.8%
```

kevin: Hmm — halluc rate roughly doubled on the longdoc slice. Is that live traffic or synthetic?

maya: Live 5% cohort, longdoc slice only, ~3k requests sampled. Also saw token-prefix mismatch in ~0.3% of those sessions.

jia: Could be kv-cache/quant desync. @deploy-bot fetch logs for a few session ids from the 5% cohort (sess ids: s-41f3, s-42b1, s-4c99).

deploy-bot: fetching logs for s-41f3, s-42b1, s-4c99... gist: https://redwood.internal/g/xyz123 (attached)

alex: If the longdoc MRR drop is real we should cut traffic. What's our current autofallback rule?

kevin: Rule summary: autofallback if (abs(halluc_rate_delta) > 0.5%) OR (relative MRR drop > 5%) on any critical slice OR (p95 latency exceeds SLA+50ms).

maya: For this run: halluc_delta = +0.9% abs, relative MRR drop = (0.82-0.78)/0.82 = 4.9% (just under 5%). Latency is better.

jia: Suggest we immediate drop the longdoc slice to 0% for the variant and keep shorttext at 5% while we triage. I'll queue an eval job that replays denser longdocs.

maya: Doing rollback for longdoc slice now. Tagging the variant as 'suspect-int4-longdoc' and leaving shorttext traffic untouched. PR with artifacts: https://redwood.internal/pr/4456

alex: +1. Also spin up a 10k longdoc offline replay and run contrastive rerank to see if the failure compounds downstream.

kevin: Also check kv warmup TTL and cache warming heuristics — quantized weights sometimes expose cold-kv prefix mismatches. Increase warmup window and re-run smoke if needed.

maya: Noted. I'll bump warmup TTL to 5s for the next run and attach updated eval logs to the PR.

jia: If we still see sustained +0.9% halluc on longdocs after warmup, policy triggers auto-fallback. I'll monitor dashboards and alert if it persists.

maya: Thanks all :thumbsup:
